fact: UNHCR's Annual Results Report 2025 says it had registered 108,455 refugees and asylum-seekers individually in Libya (40,699 of them new in 2025), with biometric enrolment of 41,157 people aged five and over, and issued asylum-seeker and refugee certificates.

UNHCR says Libyan authorities do not recognise its registration documents, authority registration in Alkufra was suspended between August and November 2025, and most Sudanese refugees in the east remain undocumented.

Carnegie Sada (Zayed) reports that western Libya's civil registries refused to register a child of a displaced eastern family, citing birth in Benghazi, leaving him without citizenship or national ID procedures and without access to education, health care or child grants; IDPs are systematically impeded in obtaining personal documents.

UNHCR reports it had registered a cumulative 79,019 refugees and asylum-seekers in Libya by the end of 2024, 36,159 of them new in 2024, at its Tripoli registration centre, with documentation (a UNHCR refugee certificate) issued to them.
system: UNHCR registration, Sarraj Registration Centre, Tripoli (proGres)

fact: UNHCR reports East-based Libyan authorities register medically cleared Sudanese new arrivals in Alkufra and issue them a Registration Security Card, which UNHCR says is not recognized in the West.

UNHCR reports that from January 2024 its Tripoli registration team used the Libya Appointment and Services System (LASS) to schedule and process registration cases, and that authorities in the West were reluctant to carry out registration themselves.
